evidence.requirements: Almost everything in the brief is implemented. The list has the heading, name links, family, L3, Search, Family select and the '<n> cartridges' count (screenshots/list.jpg, views.js:28-42). Search matches alternative names and treats ',' and '.' alike (format.js:109-117). The detail view shows the facts, the capacity with its source link, Symbol/Value/Unit tables grouped by section, tolerances beside their values, Print and All cartridges (views.js:86-152). Hash routes give each view a bookmarkable address (router.js). The SVG is labelled '<name> drawing' and has a hatched section, a dash-dot centre line, all 13 dimensions, a title block (dimensions.js:61-176, 258-267) and missing-value notes. There is one A4 print stylesheet with a footer (print.css). Partly met: (1) the printed drawing is not at full width. print.css:157 fixes the SVG at 96 mm high, so a long case is limited by height and its content fills only about 60-65% of the width (test-output/print-308_win.png). (2) On a 360 px phone the drawing labels are about 7 px high, which README:61 admits and test-output/phone-detail.png shows. (3) The check could not capture any detail or print screenshot, so the current detail view could not be verified independently.
evidence.correctness: The geometry follows the rules closely. Rim type: geometry.js:51-58. Chamfer min(f·tanβ, R1/4): geometry.js:93. Rimfire half-round with its outermost point at R1/2: geometry.js:76-86. Groove floor and ramp, and the belt ramp at δ to R3/2 then a step at E: geometry.js:103-129. Shoulder through the published points, α labelled with the published value, apex arc: geometry.js:159-175, dimensions.js:149-176. Seating and k by shape and category, tangent ogive with the stated ρ and centre, quarter ellipse, cones: bullet.js:13-79. Heeled H2-2tb seat: bullet.js:89-91. Walls, w and primer pockets: geometry.js:189-218. Compared with the references (308_win, 300_win_mag, 9_mm_luger, 22_long_rifle.png), the agent's renders have matching outlines and proportions, including the belt, the heeled 22 LR and the round-nose 9 mm. Values are printed with String(n), so '51.18' and '4150' come out as published; angles show as '10°58'0"'. Gaps: fillet tangents are capped at 45% of the adjoining segment (geometry.js:17,163), so a large r1 min such as 6,5 x 55's 3.5 is silently drawn smaller. The printed drawing uses only part of the page width. One-page print is asserted for all 25 records (tests/e2e/print.test.js:24-39), but no print screenshot of the current build exists.
evidence.security: Every innerHTML string is built from escaped data: esc() appears in every interpolation in views.js:18-168 and drawing.js:45,103,115. The capacity link is restricted to http(s) (views.js:11,79). A strict CSP sets default-src 'none' and script-src 'self' (index.html:7). There is no eval, Function, fetch or XHR (grep). The only outbound link is the source citation.
evidence.code_quality: The modules are small and pure: format, mathutil, bullet, geometry, dimensions, drawing, router, views and app, each a UMD-style IIFE that is testable in Node. Named constants replace magic numbers (geometry.js:10-20, dimensions.js:9-34). Missing values are reported through createReport. The label placement is a backtracking row search with a node cap and a staircase fallback (dimensions.js:203-236). It is sophisticated but contained. The functions are short, the names are clear and the comments are sparse and useful.
evidence.tests: Coverage is extensive. There are unit tests for every geometry rule with numeric checks (chamfer, half-round, groove, belt ramp, fillet sagitta, ogive centre and radius, ellipse equation, heeled seat, w, pockets) and for missing-value handling (tests/unit/geometry.test.js). There are layout collision tests across all 25 drawings and a check that the collision checker really detects overlaps (dimensions.test.js:98-126). The formatting tests cover tolerances, angles and symbols. The Playwright e2e tests cover file:// and a served sub-path, phone, dark mode, one A4 page per record, black-on-white print, stated versus printed scale, no network requests, CSP and focus. One weakness: 'the drawing spans the full printable width' (print.test.js:72-89) measures the SVG box, not the drawn content, so it passes while the content is narrower.
evidence.ux_design: The list is calm and readable, with right-aligned tabular L3 values and muted units (list.jpg). The rows are 44 px tall with a lot of empty width between columns, which is less dense than the brief asks. The agent's own renders show a dense detail page: a facts grid, a drawing in a framed figure and many compact tables (test-output/screen-detail-dark.png). Dark mode is well handled. The drawing labels are large and legible on desktop and do not overlap. The title block is large relative to the case. On a phone the drawing becomes tiny (phone-detail.png). The print sheet is well organised into a 5-column table grid with the facts in a header grid.
evidence.accessibility: The SVG has role=img, aria-label '<name> drawing' and aria-describedby pointing to the notes (drawing.js:115, views.js:136). Tables have captions and th scope=col/row (views.js:110-122). Inputs have labels and the filters sit in a search landmark (views.js:30-34). The count is a polite live region. There is a skip link, focus moves to the h1 on navigation (app.js:38), focus-visible outlines are set (styles.css:122) and touch targets are 44 px. The colours are chosen for contrast and e2e tests assert 3:1 control borders.
evidence.simplicity: There is no framework and no runtime dependency. The only dev dependency is playwright 1.64.1. The app is about 1,100 lines of JS for geometry, layout and views, which is proportionate to a computed technical drawing. The backtracking label search and the separate print-scale computation add some complexity, but both serve stated requirements.
evidence.maintainability: README.md covers use, layout, testing, the Chromium library workaround and known limits. Playwright is pinned exactly and package-lock.json is present. data.js is generated from the fixture and a test checks the two are identical. Missing: there is no CI configuration at all and no engines field or .nvmrc for Node 22. README:36-38 sends readers to openspec/changes/build-cartridge-reference/design.md for every interpretation, but that directory is not in the repository (only openspec/specs/.gitkeep). Version 1.0.0 has no changelog or release notes. The committed test-output PNGs are stale: they show 'Scale 1:1 … fitted to width', while dimensions.js:258 now writes 'Scale x.xx:1 on A4 print'.
evidence.visual_design: The look is consistent: paper, ink and one drafting-blue accent, small-caps labels, monospaced symbols and tabular numerals (styles.css:1-29; list.jpg). Hairline rules and table framing look finished. The drawing uses non-scaling strokes, proper arrowheads and hatch patterns at different angles for the case and the bullet. The drawing's monospaced labels are oversized relative to small pistol and rimfire cases, and the title block is wide.
evidence.layout: The list page has a clear hierarchy: heading, filters, count, then the table (list.jpg). Name and family are far apart on wide screens. In the agent's renders the detail page puts the facts first, then the drawing, then the cartridge and chamber tables in a responsive grid, with no clipping or overlap. The print sheet places everything on one page with the header, the drawing and a 5-column table grid. The drawing area wastes width and the lower part of the page is left empty (print-308_win.png). The check captured no detail or print screenshots, so the current layout could not be confirmed.
evidence.usability: Search is immediate and explains alias matches ('also: …', views.js:20). Filters survive navigation to a detail view and back. Back and forward work through hash routes. An unknown address gets a 'Cartridge not found' view with a link back. Print and All cartridges are prominent. Missing features are explained under the drawing. On phones the drawing needs pinch-zoom to read.
evidence.reception: Engineers and reloaders would trust it: it cites its source and commit, shows values exactly as published with tolerances, explains what is missing, and draws to scale with a proper section view. It looks like a professional reference. Small shortfalls are the phone drawing legibility and a print drawing that does not use the full page width.

unmet_requirements: Print: the drawing is not 'at full width'. It is fitted into a fixed 96 mm-high box (print.css:157, dimensions.js:32), so long cases fill only about 60-65% of the printable width.
Phone: the drawing scales to the screen width, but the labels are about 7 px high, too small to read without zooming (README:61, test-output/phone-detail.png).
The check captured no detail or print screenshots, so the current build's detail and print rendering could not be verified independently.
strengths: The drawing geometry follows the brief's rules precisely: chamfer, rimfire half-round, groove, belt ramp, shoulder through the published points with α, ogive, ellipse and cone noses, heeled bullet, walls, solid head and primer pockets. Missing values are reported, never invented, and the renders match the reference proportions.

Very thorough tests. Unit tests check each rule numerically. Playwright e2e tests cover all 25 records for label collisions, true scale, a one-page A4 print, black-on-white print, dark mode, phone layout, file:// and served use, no network requests and CSP.

Clean, secure, dependency-free implementation: pure modules, all markup escaped, a strict CSP, a strong accessibility setup (described SVG, captioned tables, live count, focus handling) and a calm technical visual style.
issues: The check captured no detail or print screenshots, and the committed test-output renders predate the current title-block code. The current detail and print views have not been confirmed visually.

The printed drawing is fitted to a fixed 96 mm height rather than the full page width. The test that claims full width measures the SVG box, not the drawn content. On phones the drawing labels are about 7 px high.
Maintainability gaps: no CI pipeline and no pinned Node runtime (no engines field or .nvmrc). The README points to openspec design documents that are not in the repository, and there is no changelog.
review.verdict: The rule-faithful drawing engine, exhaustive tests and secure, accessible, dependency-free code make this a technically strong cartridge reference that the target audience would trust. It needs a full-width print drawing, readable phone labels, a CI pipeline and confirmed detail and print rendering before it is published as is.
